sources.title: NGSS 3-ESS2-2: Obtain and combine information to describe climates in different regions of the world

steps.title: Earth
steps.instruction: Trace the outline of the Earth.

note.text: Earth is a sphere, so sunlight hits different places at different angles. That's why climates differ.

steps.title: Equator
steps.instruction: Draw the equator across the middle.

note.text: The equator circles Earth halfway between the poles. The sun is almost straight overhead here all year.

steps.title: Tropic lines
steps.instruction: Draw the two lines on either side of the equator.

note.text: Between these lines is the tropical zone. It's warm all year, and many places have a wet and a dry season.

steps.title: Polar circles
steps.instruction: Draw the two short lines near the top and bottom.

note.text: Beyond these lines are the polar zones. Sunlight arrives at a low slant, so it's cold all year.
note.remember: Between tropical and polar lies temperate: four seasons.

steps.title: Label the zones
steps.instruction: Pick the climate zone for each numbered spot.

targets.role: Near the equator: hot all year.
Middle latitudes: warm summers, cool winters.

mistakes.Tropical: The tropical zone hugs the equator. This spot is farther north, where seasons change.

targets.role: Near the poles: cold all year.

commonMistakes.Desert: Deserts are dry places. They're found in several zones, so desert isn't one of these three bands.

steps.title: Explain
steps.question: Why is it warmer near the equator than near the poles?

options.text: Sunlight hits the equator more directly
options.feedback: Yes. Direct rays concentrate energy on a small area. At the poles, slanted rays spread the same energy thin.

options.text: The equator is closer to the sun
options.feedback: The difference in distance is tiny. It's the angle of the sunlight that matters.

options.text: There is more land at the equator
options.feedback: Climate zones form because of sunlight angle, not how much land there is.
The poles get sunlight, but at a low angle, so it's weaker.
